Parents.title: 👨‍👩‍👧 For Parents & Teachers
Parents.whatIsText: JamboScript is a programming language designed in Swahili. It teaches basic computer science concepts through stories and games — children learn by doing, not just reading.
Parents.ageText: JamboScript is designed for children aged 8–14. No prior knowledge is required — the game teaches step by step.
Parents.safetyText: All code runs inside the browser only — no data is sent to servers. No ads, no tracking, no hidden charges.

ContextualGuide.namingQuestion: Hello, traveler. What is your name?

ch1.title: First Commands
ch1.subtitle: Learn to give your first commands
ch1.d1: In the village of Algoriti, a great gate stands sealed by magic. You must speak the right words to open it...
ch1.d2: Hey there! I'm Kito 🐢. See this gate — it's locked! To open it, the computer must "speak" words out loud.
ch1.d3: "andika" is JamboScript's first command — it tells the computer: "say this out loud!" Try it:
ch1.d4: andika(...) = show output. The words inside "..." are what gets displayed. The gate will open when you speak!
ch1.starterCode: # Write a command to open the gate
ch1.task: Write a command to open the village gate
ch1.riddle: 🚪 The gate is sealed by magic. Say the right words to open it!
ch1.hint1: Use the word "andika" followed by parentheses with words inside
ch1.hint3: Make sure you use quote marks " " around your words
ch1.errorGeneric: There's an error in your code

ch2.title: Saving & Naming
ch2.subtitle: Learn to use variables
ch2.d1: The gate is open! The village guard stands at the entrance, spear in hand. He asks: "What is your name?"
ch2.d2: The guard won't let you pass without knowing your name! We need to "save" your name in the computer's memory.
ch2.d3: "acha" is like a box — you put something inside and give it a name. Save your name like this:
ch2.d4: "acha jina = ..." = the computer remembers. "andika(jina)" = say the name out loud — the guard will hear it and let you pass!
ch2.starterCode:
# Save your name here

acha jina = ""

# Then say your name
andika(jina)
ch2.task: Give yourself a name and tell the village!
ch2.riddle: 🏠 The guard asks: "What is your name?" — Save your name in a variable!
ch2.hint1: Replace "" with your name inside the quote marks
ch2.hint3: Make sure the name has at least one character inside ""
ch2.errorGeneric: There's an error in your code
ch2.errorNoName: Save your name — write a name inside the quote marks!

ch3.title: If... Then...
ch3.subtitle: Learn to make decisions
ch3.d1: Your journey takes you into the forest. Ahead, the path splits — left is a cave, right is a river...
ch3.d2: Welcome to the forest, young one 🧙. Look — two paths! You must choose based on the weather.
ch3.d3: Computers can make decisions! "kama" = check a condition, "la sivyo" = the other option:
ch3.d4: Rain? → safe cave 🕳️. Sun? → beautiful river 🏞️. "kama" is like a brain — it checks the condition, then chooses!
ch3.task: Choose the right path based on the weather
ch3.riddle: 🌧️ Rain or sun? Choose the right path for the weather!
ch3.hint1: "kama" is the same as "if" — check a condition inside parentheses
ch3.hint3: "la sivyo" is the same as "else" — the other option
ch3.errorGeneric: There's an error in your code
ch3.errorNoPath: Make sure you saved the path in a variable called "njia"

ch4.title: Repeat Again
ch4.subtitle: Learn to repeat commands
ch4.d1: Ahead is a rope bridge over a river. See the 5 planks — you must cross one step at a time...
ch4.d2: This bridge is fragile! Only 5 planks. Take one step at a time — but you don't need to write the command 5 times!
ch4.d3: "rudia" is a powerful command — it says "do this 5 times" in one line! Watch:
ch4.d4: Proverb: "One step at a time, the journey is completed." Use a loop to cross!
ch4.task: Use a loop to walk 5 steps across the bridge
ch4.riddle: 🌉 Rope bridge — only 5 steps. Use "rudia" to cross safely!
ch4.hint1: "rudia" is the same as "for" — it repeats commands many times
ch4.hint2: Start with i = 0, repeat while i chini 5, i++ each time
ch4.hint3: Inside {}, write the command to walk
ch4.errorGeneric: There's an error in your code
ch4.errorNoVar: Make sure you have a variable called "hatua"
ch4.errorTooMany: Too many steps! The bridge will break!
ch4.errorTooFew: Not enough steps to cross the bridge!
ch4.errorNotNumber: Make sure hatua is the number 5

ch5.title: My Functions
ch5.subtitle: Learn to create functions
ch5.d1: You've reached the top of the mountain! Here, characters learn to create their own magic — functions...
ch5.d2: See this magic box! "kazi" is like a machine — you create it once, then use it many times. Give it something, it returns an answer!
ch5.d3: "kazi" = create new magic. "rudisha" = return an answer. Give it 7, it returns double:
ch5.d4: The box receives 7, multiplies × 2, returns 14. That's a "kazi" — magic that returns answers! Try it.
ch5.task: Create a function that doubles a number
ch5.riddle: ⛰️ On the mountain, magic multiplies you! Create a "maraMbili" function — give it a number, it returns double!
ch5.hint1: "kazi" is the same as "function" — to create new magic
ch5.hint2: "rudisha" is the same as "return" — to give back an answer
ch5.errorGeneric: There's an error in your code
ch5.errorNoVar: Make sure you have a variable called "jibu"
ch5.errorWrongAnswer: The answer should be 14, but you got something else
